reviews.rationale: Selected-row sequential comparison of the Q2 and Q3 earnings exhibits shows a mixed picture that does not resolve into a defensible directional view. GAAP operating income turned positive and the GAAP net loss narrowed, but the improvement is dominated by a swing in the signed other operating expense (income), net line rather than by operating leverage: total operating expenses fell while cost of revenues rose, so the expense decline is not attributable to the core cost base. Company-defined adjusted EBITDA and adjusted net income both declined, which is directionally opposed to the GAAP operating improvement and indicates the non-GAAP view of underlying profitability did not strengthen. Revenue was roughly flat, with recurring revenue components softening and transactional revenue and the Academia & Government segment offsetting declines in Intellectual Property and Life Sciences & Healthcare; the mix shift toward transactional and segment concentration is not explained by the selected rows. Cash generation improved materially on both GAAP operating cash flow and company-defined free cash flow, but working-capital and timing effects are not visible in the extract, so the durability of the cash improvement is unverified. The tax provision decreased while pretax loss narrowed, and the relationship between the two is not explained by the selected rows. Because the GAAP improvement appears driven by a non-recurring-looking other operating line, the non-GAAP measures moved the other way, and the selected extract lacks segment drivers, reconciliations, working-capital detail, and any guidance or consensus context, the evidence is insufficient to upgrade or downgrade the thesis. Research state is held for review pending the full filing, non-GAAP reconciliations, and management commentary.
